questions.text: Which standardized survey is used to measure inpatient patients' perspectives on hospital care in the United States?
questions.explanation: HCAHPS (Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems) is the national, standardized, publicly reported survey of patients' perspectives on hospital care.

questions.text: Patient-centered care is BEST defined as care that:

options.a: Prioritizes clinical outcomes above all other considerations
options.b: Respects and responds to individual patient preferences, needs, and values
options.c: Standardizes care protocols to reduce variation
options.d: Focuses exclusively on preventing medical errors

questions.explanation: Patient-centered care places the patient's preferences, needs, and values at the center of all clinical decisions, as defined by the IOM.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a 'patient engagement' strategy?

options.a: Restricting family member visits to reduce infection risk
options.b: Inviting patients to participate in bedside shift reports
options.c: Requiring patients to sign consent forms

questions.explanation: Bedside shift reports involving patients directly engage them in their care, improving communication and safety.

questions.text: A hospital receives consistently low scores on the 'communication about medicines' domain of HCAHPS. Which intervention would MOST directly address this?

options.a: Increasing nursing staff on all units
options.b: Training nurses to explain medications, side effects, and reasons using teach-back
options.c: Distributing printed medication lists to all patients
options.d: Reducing the number of medications prescribed per patient

questions.explanation: Using teach-back and clear communication techniques when explaining medications directly addresses the HCAHPS domain measuring how well staff communicate about medicines.

options.a: A patient's ability to pay for healthcare services
options.b: A patient's ability to obtain, process, and understand basic health information
options.c: The level of education required to work in healthcare
options.d: A clinician's knowledge of public health topics

questions.explanation: Health literacy is the degree to which individuals can obtain, process, and understand health information needed to make appropriate decisions.

questions.text: Which of the following strategies is MOST effective for improving patient satisfaction with pain management?

options.a: Ensuring all patients receive opioid pain medications
options.b: Proactively assessing and addressing pain, and communicating the pain management plan to patients
options.d: Eliminating pain scales from patient assessments

questions.explanation: Proactive pain assessment, combined with clear communication of the pain management plan, has the greatest impact on patient satisfaction with pain care.

options.a: Train nursing students during clinical rotations
options.b: Confirm that patients understand the information they have been given
options.c: Document patient education in the EHR

questions.explanation: Teach-back asks patients to explain in their own words what they were told, confirming understanding and allowing clinicians to correct any misunderstandings.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered a dimension of patient-centered care according to the Picker Institute?

options.b: Respect for patients' values, preferences, and expressed needs

questions.explanation: The Picker Institute identified eight dimensions of patient-centered care, with respect for patients' values, preferences, and needs as a core dimension.

questions.text: A hospital wants to increase its HCAHPS 'top box' scores. 'Top box' scores refer to:

options.a: The percentage of patients giving the highest possible rating
options.b: The total number of surveys returned
options.c: The average score across all domains

questions.explanation: Top box scores represent the percentage of patients who selected the most positive response category (e.g., 'Always' or '9 or 10'), which is how HCAHPS results are publicly reported.

questions.text: Patient experience is DIFFERENT from patient satisfaction in that:

options.a: Patient satisfaction is objective while experience is subjective
options.b: Patient experience measures what actually happened during care; satisfaction measures how patients felt about it
options.c: Patient satisfaction is measured by clinical outcomes
options.d: Patient experience only applies to inpatient settings

questions.explanation: Patient experience captures specific events and interactions during care; satisfaction measures the patient's emotional reaction to those events, which is influenced by expectations.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST supports shared decision-making between patients and providers?

options.a: Providing patients with a single recommended treatment option
options.b: Presenting patients with evidence-based options and incorporating their preferences into the plan
options.c: Having the physician make all treatment decisions to avoid patient confusion
options.d: Using standardized care pathways without exceptions

questions.explanation: Shared decision-making involves presenting evidence-based options, discussing benefits and risks, and incorporating the patient's values and preferences into the final care plan.

questions.text: A quality team reviews HCAHPS results and finds a significant drop in 'responsiveness of hospital staff' scores. Which intervention should be PRIORITIZED?
questions.explanation: Hourly rounding proactively addresses patient needs, reducing call light use and improving responsiveness scores — consistently one of the most effective interventions for this domain.

questions.text: Cultural competence in healthcare is BEST described as:

options.a: The ability to speak multiple languages
options.b: The capacity to provide effective care that meets the cultural, social, and linguistic needs of patients
options.c: Following all patients' requests regardless of clinical appropriateness
options.d: Eliminating cultural differences in care delivery

questions.explanation: Cultural competence involves providing care that is respectful of and responsive to the health beliefs, practices, and cultural and linguistic needs of diverse patients.

questions.text: Which approach BEST reduces patient anxiety prior to a procedure?

options.a: Avoiding discussion of risks to prevent patient distress
options.b: Providing clear, tailored information about what to expect before, during, and after the procedure
options.c: Administering sedation as early as possible
options.d: Limiting family involvement to reduce distractions

questions.explanation: Clear, individualized preparation information reduces uncertainty and anxiety by helping patients know what to expect throughout the care process.

questions.text: A hospital's patient advisory council includes former patients who contribute to care improvement decisions. This is an example of:

options.b: Patient and family engagement in quality improvement

questions.explanation: Patient and family advisory councils are a structured form of patient and family engagement in organizational quality improvement and decision-making.
